title: onCleanup
summary: Run a function once when a cleanup object is deleted or its last reachable owner is released.

gpu_support.notes: Host-side lifecycle helper. Callback bodies may call GPU-aware functions, but the cleanup object itself does not launch kernels.

description: `onCleanup(f)` creates a handle object that invokes the zero-input function handle `f` on explicit deletion or when its last reachable owner is released. Clearing one workspace name does not run the callback while another alias or active capture still owns the object. It is useful for restoring state, closing files, removing temporary folders, and other cleanup tasks.
behaviors: `cleanupObj = onCleanup(cleanupFun)` requires `cleanupFun` to be a function handle or anonymous-function closure.
The cleanup function is invoked with zero input arguments and zero requested outputs.
The callback runs at most once for each cleanup object.
`delete(cleanupObj)` invokes the callback immediately through the onCleanup handle method.
`cancel(cleanupObj)` deactivates the cleanup object without invoking the callback.

`clear cleanupObj`, `clear`, and `clearvars` detach the selected workspace bindings first. An active callback runs once when no other alias, capture, pending operation, or external root still owns the object.
A normal hosted session drains admitted callbacks before graceful close. Forced disposal can abandon a queued callback; it does not replay an already admitted callback.

faqs.question: Can I pass arguments directly to the cleanup function?
faqs.answer: No. Use an anonymous function that captures the values you need, for example `onCleanup(@() fclose(fid))`.

faqs.question: Does the callback run more than once if I call delete multiple times?
faqs.answer: No. The object is deactivated before the callback is invoked, so later delete, clear, or clearvars paths are no-ops.

faqs.question: Does `cancel` delete the object?
faqs.answer: `cancel` only deactivates the callback. The handle value can still exist, but it will no longer run the cleanup function.

faqs.question: Will clearing one name run cleanup if another name holds the same object?
faqs.answer: No. Cleanup waits until the last reachable owner is released, or until the object is explicitly deleted.

faqs.question: Does GPU residency matter?
faqs.answer: No. The cleanup handle is a host object. Any GPU work is determined by the callback body itself.

gpu_behavior: `onCleanup` creates and manages a host lifecycle object. It does not participate in fusion and does not create GPU-resident outputs.
